Hi I realized the problem is caused by the difference of episode lengths The LSTM version algorithms I implemented require the episode length to be the same for all episodes and the sample is saved in an episodic manner here https github com quantumiracle Popular RL Algorithms blob c7200d1072c50bc99d6e82f10ff2d62a3353247c sac v2 lstm py L284 This is okay for the environments I tested e g Reacher Pendulum v0 HalfCheetah v2 without failure states but for BipedalWalker there is the failure state when the bot falls onto the ground that will terminate the episode which makes episode length different for each episode Thus the sampled data here https github com quantumiracle Popular RL Algorithms blob c7200d1072c50bc99d6e82f10ff2d62a3353247c sac v2 lstm py L106 will not be a valid tensor thus this line will return such error See some previous discussions and solutions 20 But this is not implemented in the current repo it should be not hard to do that

title: Random actions at the beginning for recurrent policy
body: Hello I wonder what you would implement to achieve the above thing It is easy in the mdp policy but for recurrent policies how we can get the hidden out if we take a random action For instance if we take the action from the policy net then we can get hidden out but what if we take a random action action hidden out sac trainer policy net get action obs last action hidden in deterministic environment deterministic train

comments.body: Hi If you take a look at how the SAC LSTM version saves samples in replay buffer here https github com quantumiracle Popular RL Algorithms blob 46a1af759ba77afae9d8bcfa6a73e76c8577c1fb sac v2 lstm py L284 and how it uses samples for updating here https github com quantumiracle Popular RL Algorithms blob 46a1af759ba77afae9d8bcfa6a73e76c8577c1fb sac v2 lstm py L103 you will find only the initial hidden inputs and initial hidden outputs in each episode are stored in the buffer So your question will only concern with one transition in random exploration stage for each episode At present I do not have a mature idea for getting a theoretically correct hidden out for random case but I guess it won t affect too much of the performance in general due to the fact that the subsequent actions after the initial one are also random therefore not relying on the hidden out

title: Variable length episodes
body: I tried to use you code on a custom environment that can have vaiable length episodes Maybe I have set it up wrong but I can t figure out how it can work The replay buffer is filled from complete episodes not just state transitions but in update in the td3 lstm it samples those episodes and uses torch FloatTensor state to device to put it to the GPU but this wont work as the batch can have varying length episodes and pytorch wont allow this Possibly works on a batch size of 1

comments.body: Hi I think what you said is correct For lstm version the whole episode of transitions are sent to train the policy as a single sample Variate length of episodes can be achieved with two ways 1 padding consecutive transitions with zeros in episode if it has a different length from other episodes the maximal one however the zero padding may not make sense in some cases 2 change the update manner of lstm policy to take one transition at a time but keep the gradients of hidden states not detached so that it can be tracked along the episode Also welcome to contribute some other implementations for achieving that
